thread:
Aoife: heads-up: pool3 started showing ECC bursts on 3 cards over the last 40m, but pattern is weird — short saturated bursts during small inference jobs, then quiet. logs attached here (copied snippets).
Sanjay: can you paste the raw nvml/mm logs? are Xid codes present or just correctables?
Aoife: mostly correctables, occasional Xid 13. snippet:
```
GPU 5: ECC_CORRECTABLE 62 -> 0 diff 62
GPU 7: ECC_CORRECTABLE 48 -> 0 diff 48
nvml: Xid 13 @ 0x7f1a3f
```
Miguel: hmm that burstiness during tiny jobs smells like PCI negotiation or a fabric hiccup, not a dying card. Did the recent BIOS/firmware rollout hit these hosts?
Aoife: checked — firmware matches baseline. these hosts landed the new driver 530.41 last week.
Li: 530.x had one regression on some rigs, but we've seen that with longer seq lengths, not tiny jobs. worth checking link speeds and pcie errors.
Priya: best short-term mitigation is to avoid immediate replace. can we try a soft-drain policy that marks cards as degraded and routes new jobs away, but leaves current pods to finish? soft-drain + increased monitoring window.
Sanjay: agree. open question: what signal should trigger soft-drain? currently we use 1-min correctable rate > 20 -> immediate drain, which is noisy. propose a "burstiness score": count of sub-1min spikes / weighted recent spike count.
Aoife: proposed rule: compute burstiness = number_of_spikes_in_15m / max(1, sustained_errors_in_60m). if burstiness > 0.6 AND at least 3 spikes in 15m -> soft-drain. else if sustained_errors_60m > 100 or Xid present -> hard-evac.
Miguel: that would avoid draining for single transient bursts. also add host-level backoff: don't replace/retire a card unless it's been soft-drained 24h and still produces high sustained errors.
Priya: can infra-bot tag affected hosts so scheduler ignores them for new jobs? we need a command we can hit quickly.
infra-bot: @priya tagging hosts: pool3-host-17, pool3-host-21, pool3-host-29 as "degraded-ecc-1749456789". scheduler routing rules updated to prefer non-degraded with 5% fallback allowed. :white_check_mark:
Li: quick repro idea: run small 1-2 token echo loops at p99 concurrency to try to trigger bursts. if we can reproduce, we can link to kernel logs and raise with driver vendor.
Sanjay: operational checklist for this incident:
- short term: apply soft-drain policy (burstiness rule) for pool3; roll rollback window 2h
- med term: run repro job across the three hosts for 6h
- long term: add new telemetry: 10s-window correctable histogram (to compute burstiness), and make the threshold configurable per-region
Aoife: adding cost note: soft-drain will reduce immediate capacity in pool3 by ~6% because scheduler avoids degraded hosts. acceptable for next 24h.
Priya: I'm creating a quick runbook PR with the policy and the command to tag/untag. will also add a one-click run for the repro job in console.
Miguel: add a guard: if any host shows Xid >= 1 in the last 12h, auto-promote to hard-evac with alert to oncall.
Aoife: agreed. one more: alert suppression so we don't spam oncall during the soft-drain observation window — aggregate notifications to one digest per pool per 30m.
Sanjay: I'll push a hotfix to the monitoring pipeline (k8s daemon) to emit the burstiness metric and to the autoscaling policy hooks. ETA 3h.
Priya: tagging owners on tasks: @sanjay (monitoring hotfix), @li (repro job + kernel logs), @miguel (scheduling/capacity impact), @aoife (incident owner + vendor escalation if repro confirmed).
Aoife: thanks all. leaving the degraded tag in place for now; update here when repro job finishes or we see hard-evac triggers. :thumbsup:
